identity.operation: Call utf8proc_map with an explicit input length.
identity.condition: Valid UTF-8 bytes follow an embedded NUL within that length.
identity.capability: Process the bytes after the NUL.
identity.consequence: Those bytes are excluded from mapping.

requirement: Exercise explicit-length mapping of valid UTF-8 bytes after an embedded NUL.

assessment.necessity_reason: The utf8proc_map contract supports an explicit length containing an embedded NUL. A finite input such as A\0B\0 passes the harness guards, but every explicit map call receives strlen(data), which ends before B.

before.requirement: Call utf8proc_map with an explicit length that includes valid UTF-8 bytes after an embedded NUL.
before.reason: The before contract permits this input, but the harness derives every explicit map length from strlen(data). Its normalization shortcuts stop at the NUL, so they provide no equivalent route.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Decomposition processes the supplied byte length when UTF8PROC_NULLTERM is absent.
The normalization shortcuts invoke mapping with UTF8PROC_NULLTERM.

after.requirement: Call utf8proc_map with an explicit length that includes valid UTF-8 bytes after an embedded NUL.
after.reason: The same explicit-length contract remains, and the fixed old harness still passes strlen(data) to every explicit map call.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Decomposition still processes the supplied byte length when UTF8PROC_NULLTERM is absent.
The normalization shortcuts still invoke mapping with UTF8PROC_NULLTERM.

assessment.comparison_reason: The obligation and source contract are the same on both sides. The unchanged strlen-derived map length is the same concrete blocker.

necessity_evidence.reason: The same target coverage gap is preexisting on both sides of g0002. Explicit-length mapping supports bytes after an embedded NUL, but the fixed harness passes strlen(data) to every utf8proc_map call.
necessity_evidence.finite_witness: Input bytes [0x41, 0x00, 0x42, 0x00], size 4, pass the entry guards. The supported call utf8proc_map(data, 3, ...) would process B after the embedded NUL; the harness instead computes len = 1 and passes 1 to every map call.

scope_contract.reason: utf8proc_map is a primary target operation. Its unchanged before and after contract accepts an explicit byte length and permits NUL characters within the input.

feasible_trigger.reason: The four-byte witness passes the size and final-NUL guards. Without UTF8PROC_NULLTERM, decomposition processes the supplied length, including the embedded NUL and following valid ASCII byte; the harness's strlen-derived length blocks that supported setup.

evidence.dependency_reason: Shows that explicit-length decomposition continues until the supplied length.

observable_consequence.reason: For any input containing an embedded NUL, every actual explicit map call ends its input at that NUL, so the supported behavior of mapping subsequent bytes is unreachable.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete entry has no map call using a length beyond strlen(data). Its normalization shortcuts use UTF8PROC_NULLTERM, and its UTF-32 normalization calls do not perform the frozen explicit-length utf8proc_map operation.

evidence.dependency_reason: Shows the normalization shortcuts invoke NULLTERM mapping.

identity_preserved.reason: The same explicit-length utf8proc_map tuple is required before and after; the unchanged harness uses the same strlen-derived length on both sides.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: utf8proc_map processes valid UTF-8 bytes after an embedded NUL when they fall within its explicit input length.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Call utf8proc_map without UTF8PROC_NULLTERM, passing a length that includes the embedded NUL and following bytes.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: Every explicit map call passes len = strlen(data).
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: No explicit map call processes the bytes after the first NUL.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: None in the complete entry: normalization shortcuts use UTF8PROC_NULLTERM, and UTF-32 normalization is a different operation.
